title: {Syn} CRISPR Turns Bacterial Defense Into Gene Editing
content:
CRISPR-Cas systems originally function as adaptive immune machinery in bacteria and archaea. Scientists adapted parts of that system for targeted genome editing.

The key idea is programmable guidance: a guide RNA can help direct a Cas enzyme to a matching DNA sequence.

Why it matters: science facts keeps producing ideas that are simple enough to state and strong enough to build with.
